label: Retained projectile chance
description: Chance that a penetrating gunshot leaves a retained projectile. Raising this makes extraction necessary more often before a wound can be sutured; bandaging alone does not remove it.

label: Bandage minimum wear time (seconds)
description: Shortest resting lifetime of a dressing before its wound can reopen. The actual lifetime is chosen between the minimum and maximum; movement wears the dressing faster.

label: Bandage maximum wear time (seconds)
description: Longest resting lifetime of a dressing before its wound can reopen. Increase this for more durable bandaging; sutured wounds use permanent closure instead of this timer.

label: Walking dressing wear multiplier
description: How quickly walking wears a dressing compared with resting. A value of 1 uses resting wear; larger values bring reopening forward.

label: Running dressing wear multiplier
description: How quickly running wears a dressing compared with resting. Larger values make repeated running reopen unsutured wounds sooner.

label: Reopened wound bleeding fraction
description: Fraction of the original bleeding rate remaining when a dressed wound reopens. Lower values make recurrent bleeding slower; reopening still requires reassessment and treatment.

label: Head and torso surgery requires facility
description: Require a nearby BCM medical facility for surgery on the head, chest and abdomen. Turning this off permits eligible field surgery; definitive fracture repair still requires a facility.

label: Unsplinted leg movement fraction
description: Movement fraction allowed with an unsupported broken leg. Lower values make casualties much slower; a broken leg continues to prevent jumping.

label: Splinted leg movement fraction
description: Movement fraction allowed after a broken leg is supported by a splint. A splint improves mobility without healing the fracture or removing movement-related internal blood loss.

label: Splinted walking internal loss (ml/s)
description: Internal blood loss per second while walking on a splinted broken leg. Raise this to make walking more costly; definitive facility treatment repairs the fracture.

label: Splinted running internal loss (ml/s)
description: Internal blood loss per second while running on a splinted broken leg. This is separate from external bleeding and is not stopped by a dressing.

label: BCM depletion grace (seconds)
description: Time available in the BCM blood-depletion state before irreversible death. Restoring sufficient circulating reserve during this window can permit rescue; it does not repair untreated injuries.

label: Body bag rope length (metres)
description: Desired separation between a player and a body bag attached by a tow strap. Longer straps let the bag trail farther behind; safety release still applies.

label: Rope safety release distance (metres)
description: Maximum separation before a body-bag strap releases for safety. Prevents teleports or a stuck bag from pulling across very large distances.

label: Conscious carry consent timeout (seconds)
description: Time a conscious casualty has to answer a carry request. Reserved for the conscious-carry workflow, which is not connected yet; changing it currently has no gameplay effect.

label: Suppression enabled
description: Enable BCM suppression from qualifying near misses. Disabling this removes BCM suppression effects without changing medical injuries or the separate focus controls.

label: Suppression release (seconds)
description: Time over which accumulated suppression fades after incoming fire stops. Longer values keep the effect visible for longer; additional qualifying fire can refresh it.

label: Suppression blur (%)
description: Base strength of BCM suppression blur. Higher percentages obscure the view more; the separate blur multiplier scales this intensity.

label: Suppression vignette (%)
description: Base strength of darkened screen edges during suppression. Higher percentages produce a stronger effect; the separate vignette multiplier scales it.

label: Suppression blur multiplier
description: Additional scale applied to suppression blur strength. Zero suppresses this visual component while leaving the other suppression components enabled.

label: Suppression vignette multiplier
description: Additional scale applied to suppression edge darkening. Zero suppresses this component without disabling blur or the suppression system.

label: Limit player lives
description: Enable the BCM deployment-life limit. The current native spawn/death adapter uses the life ledger; full backend reconnect and per-account persistence acceptance remain unfinished.

label: Total lives including initial deployment
description: Total deployments available, including the initial deployment. A value of 1 represents one life; this setting does not itself implement persistent account balances.

label: Focus budget enabled
description: Enable the BCM time-limited focus budget. The duration and cooldown controls determine how long extra focus lasts and when it becomes available again.

label: Extra focus strength (%)
description: Strength of additional BCM focus while its budget is available. Raising it increases the requested focus effect; duration and cooldown are controlled separately.

label: Focus maximum duration (0 unlimited)
description: Maximum continuous duration of extra focus. Set 0 for unlimited duration; otherwise the player must release focus and satisfy the cooldown after exhaustion.

label: Focus cooldown (seconds)
description: Delay before another extra-focus activation after the previous activation ends. A longer cooldown makes repeated use less frequent.

label: Vehicle cargo interaction range (metres)
description: Search radius from the body bag for usable vehicle cargo. Applies to trucks, jeeps, ambulances and helicopters with suitable native inventory storage; it never places bags in passenger seats.

label: Maximum loading vehicle speed (m/s)
description: Highest vehicle speed allowed when loading or unloading a body bag. Lower values require the vehicle to be closer to stationary.

label: Nominal blood volume (mL)
description: Nominal full blood volume used to convert normalized native reserve into millilitres. This scales BCM blood-loss and fluid calculations; it does not create blood-type compatibility rules.

label: Resting heart rate
description: Baseline pulse for an otherwise stable patient, in beats per minute. Blood loss and active medication effects modify the simulated value.

label: Resting systolic pressure
description: Baseline systolic blood pressure for a stable patient. Poor perfusion, chest tension and medication can reduce or modify the resulting pressure.

label: Resting respiratory rate
description: Baseline spontaneous breathing rate, in breaths per minute. Oxygen deficit, airway obstruction and medication alter the simulated respiratory rate.

label: Oxygen response per second
description: Maximum change in normalized oxygen saturation per second. Higher values make deterioration and recovery react faster to ventilation, airway and lung conditions.

label: Circulatory arrest blood fraction
description: Blood-reserve fraction at or below which critical exposure can lead to cardiac arrest. The arrest-onset timer must also expire; this is a gameplay threshold, not a clinical rule.

label: Hypoxic arrest oxygen fraction
description: Oxygen-saturation fraction at or below which critical exposure can lead to cardiac arrest. The arrest-onset timer controls how long this deficit must persist.

label: Unconscious oxygen fraction
description: Oxygen threshold used by BCM hypoxia and recovery checks. Lower values allow more severe oxygen deficit before the configured unconsciousness/recovery criteria apply.

label: Critical-state time before arrest (seconds)
description: Continuous time in a critically low blood or oxygen state before arrest begins. Longer values provide a larger treatment window before spontaneous circulation is lost.

label: CPR perfusion fraction
description: Fraction of normal perfusion supplied by effective ongoing compressions. CPR remains limited by blood reserve and chest tension and does not guarantee circulation returns.

label: Corrected reversible causes before ROSC (seconds)
description: Time corrected reversible causes and effective compressions must remain stable before circulation can return. A shock alone does not satisfy the recovery conditions.

label: Maximum hypoxic injury debt (seconds)
description: Maximum accumulated injury from insufficient oxygen delivery before terminal deterioration. Severe deficits accumulate debt faster; adequate delivery allows gradual recovery.

label: Bagging duration (seconds)
description: Time required to place a deceased casualty into a body bag. The server reserves the casualty and original folded bag; interrupted operations must not duplicate equipment.

label: Bagging interaction range (metres)
description: Maximum actor-to-casualty distance for body-bag interactions. Increasing this allows bagging from farther away, subject to the other access checks.

label: Treatment interaction range (metres)
description: Maximum ground-treatment reach between medic and patient. Line of sight and actor state are also checked; viewing another vehicle occupant does not automatically allow ground procedures.

label: Examination duration (seconds)
description: Base time for a clinical examination such as checking bleeding or pulse. The progress bar follows the server timer, and a medic role applies its configured time reduction.

label: CPR communication lease (seconds)
description: Maximum interval without a valid owner CPR heartbeat before the server releases compressions. Protects against disconnected players leaving an indefinitely active CPR session.

label: Bag follow speed limit (metres/second)
description: Maximum follow speed used by a body bag during towing. This caps bag motion rather than directly setting the player movement speed.

label: Bag follow responsiveness
description: How quickly the body bag corrects its position toward the towing point. Higher values follow more tightly but may look abrupt around obstacles; lower values trail more softly.

label: Manual drag movement limit (metres/second)
description: Player movement-speed limit while manually dragging a bag. Strap towing uses a separate follow behaviour so it can support ordinary movement.

label: Dropped casualty equipment recovery radius (metres)
description: Radius used to recover recorded casualty equipment dropped nearby at death. Only eligible recorded items are considered; unrelated gear and items already taken by someone else are excluded.

label: Splint application time (seconds)
description: Base time to fit a splint to a broken leg. Treatment must finish before its kit is consumed; the medic time reduction applies.

label: Treatment movement tolerance (metres)
description: Maximum displacement from the starting position during a timed procedure. Exceeding it interrupts treatment and retains unconsumed supplies; movement-key cancellation can stop animations sooner.

label: Surgery procedure time (seconds)
description: Base time for one extraction or surgical repair procedure. Surgery does not also suture a wound, and applicable role/facility checks remain required.

label: Suture procedure time (seconds)
description: Base time to close an eligible wound with a suture kit. Retained projectiles and uncontrolled bleeding must be addressed first; the medic time reduction applies.

label: Medical facility treatment radius (metres)
description: Distance within which both actor and patient must be to use a BCM medical facility. Used by facility-restricted surgery and definitive fracture repair.

label: Bandage application time (seconds)
description: Base time to apply a native field dressing to the selected region. The original item is consumed on successful treatment, and the medic time reduction applies.

label: Pain per open wound (game units)
description: Pain contribution of each open wound in BCM game units. Dressing and suturing scale this contribution rather than automatically removing every source of pain.

label: Dressed wound pain multiplier
description: Fraction of wound pain remaining after bandaging. Lower values make dressings more effective for wound-related pain without treating fractures or internal injury.

label: Closed wound pain multiplier
description: Fraction of wound pain remaining after durable surgical closure. This affects wound pain only and does not erase other injuries.

label: Pain per unsupported fracture (game units)
description: Pain contribution of an unsupported broken leg in BCM game units. Supporting it with a splint reduces this using the separate splint multiplier.

label: Splinted fracture pain multiplier
description: Fraction of fracture pain remaining after splinting. A smaller value gives greater relief while leaving the fracture and movement restrictions in place.

label: Pain per active internal injury (game units)
description: Pain contribution of an active internal injury. External dressings do not remove this source; the relevant internal injury must be treated.

label: Medication application time (seconds)
description: Base time to administer one medication item. The server reserves the exact supply and rechecks eligibility before delivery; medics use their configured time reduction.

label: Minimum repeat interval per medication (seconds)
description: Minimum interval between administrations of the same medication to one patient. Different medication types have separate repeat histories; active-dose limits still apply.

label: Maximum concurrent doses per medication
description: Maximum concurrent active doses of one medication in a patient. Lower limits restrict stacking; elapsed doses clear according to their own onset and duration controls.

label: Morphine onset time (seconds)
description: Time for morphine to reach its maximum simulated effect after administration. A longer onset gives a slower response; this is a game-tuned effect curve, not a real dose instruction.

label: Morphine effect duration (seconds)
description: Time over which morphine fades after reaching its maximum simulated effect. Longer values keep each dose active for longer and can increase overlap with repeat administrations.

label: Morphine pain relief per active dose (game units)
description: Maximum analgesic contribution per fully active morphine dose. Relief ramps up and fades with the dose and does not stop blood loss or repair fractures.

label: Morphine breathing suppression per active dose
description: Breathing suppression per fully active morphine dose. Stacked opioid effects can worsen oxygenation; naloxone temporarily suppresses the active opioid contribution.

label: Morphine pressure suppression per active dose
description: Fractional pressure reduction per fully active morphine dose. Combined doses can worsen pressure without directly changing the underlying injury.

label: Naloxone onset time (seconds)
description: Time for naloxone to reach its maximum simulated effect after administration. A longer onset gives a slower response; this is a game-tuned effect curve, not a real dose instruction.

label: Naloxone effect duration (seconds)
description: Time over which naloxone fades after reaching its maximum simulated effect. Longer values keep each dose active for longer and can increase overlap with repeat administrations.

label: Naloxone opioid suppression per active dose
description: Fraction of active opioid effects suppressed by each fully active naloxone dose. Opioid effects can return when naloxone fades while the original opioid remains active.

label: Epinephrine onset time (seconds)
description: Time for epinephrine to reach its maximum simulated effect after administration. A longer onset gives a slower response; this is a game-tuned effect curve, not a real dose instruction.

label: Epinephrine effect duration (seconds)
description: Time over which epinephrine fades after reaching its maximum simulated effect. Longer values keep each dose active for longer and can increase overlap with repeat administrations.

label: Epinephrine pulse increase per active dose
description: Pulse increase from each fully active epinephrine dose while spontaneous circulation exists. It does not manufacture a pulse in cardiac arrest.

label: Epinephrine pressure increase per active dose
description: Pressure increase from fully active epinephrine, scaled by available perfusion. It does not replace lost blood or resolve an obstructive chest injury.

label: Maximum pain contribution to native aiming damage
description: Largest additional native aiming impairment caused by BCM pain. Analgesia can reduce this contribution, while structural arm injury remains a separate limitation.

label: Chest seal application time (seconds)
description: Base time to apply a chest seal. A seal closes an open chest wound but does not relieve existing tension. The medic time reduction applies.

label: Decompression procedure time (seconds)
description: Base time to perform needle decompression. Decompression relieves tension without repairing the original chest wound. The medic time reduction applies.

label: Airway adjunct insertion time (seconds)
description: Base time to insert an airway adjunct. The adjunct treats eligible soft-tissue obstruction in an unresponsive casualty. The medic time reduction applies.

label: Airway suction time (seconds)
description: Base time to suction an obstructed airway. Suction addresses foreign material rather than soft-tissue collapse. The medic time reduction applies.

label: Assisted ventilation action time (seconds)
description: Base time to perform one assisted ventilation cycle. A completed cycle supplies the separately configured support interval. The medic time reduction applies.

label: Ventilation support per completed cycle (seconds)
description: Length of assisted ventilation support delivered by one completed BVM cycle. Support is finite and requires a patent airway; it does not restore circulation by itself.

label: Chest drain insertion time (seconds)
description: Base time to insert a chest drain. An installed drain removes collected pleural blood without repairing its source. The medic time reduction applies.

label: Installed drain removal rate (game ml per second)
description: Rate at which an installed drain removes collected pleural blood. Draining improves the chest compartment but does not repair the bleeding source or return blood to circulation.

label: Lung recovery after corrected chest cause (fraction per second)
description: Recovery rate of a collapsed lung after the relevant air leak and tension are corrected. Faster values shorten recovery; untreated chest problems can still prevent it.

label: AED pad application time (seconds)
description: Base time to attach AED pads. Pads must be installed before analysis and discharge. The medic time reduction applies.

label: AED analysis time (seconds)
description: Base time to analyse the cardiac rhythm with an AED. Advice is tied to that device and expires after the analysis-validity interval. The medic time reduction applies.

label: AED stand-clear and discharge time (seconds)
description: Base time to complete an AED discharge sequence. Ongoing compressions and non-shockable rhythms prevent discharge. The medic time reduction applies.

label: Maximum shock analysis age (seconds)
description: How long an AED rhythm analysis remains valid for a shock decision. Advice is tied to the analysing device and the current rhythm is rechecked before discharge.

label: Available discharges per AED device
description: Available discharges in an AED item. Each completed shock uses one charge; pads and valid shockable-rhythm analysis are still required.

label: Instrumented vital check time (seconds)
description: Base time to take an instrumented monitor snapshot. The requesting player receives numerical pulse, oxygen, pressure and breathing results. The medic time reduction applies.

label: Vascular access insertion time (seconds)
description: Base time to establish vascular access. Fluids require this access and their own separate administration procedure. The medic time reduction applies.

label: Fluid bag delivery time (seconds)
description: Base time to administer one saline, plasma or whole-blood bag. Its measured volume and composition are delivered at successful completion rather than progressively; the medic time reduction applies.

label: Fluid reserve delivered by one bag (game ml)
description: Capacity assigned to newly spawned fluid bags. Saline, plasma and whole blood deliver progressively during a valid infusion; interruption preserves partial contents. Existing bags keep their original capacity when this default changes.

label: Chest penetration injury chance at full impact
description: Chance a penetrating chest impact generates the BCM open-chest/lung injury model. Higher values create these complications more often; wound bleeding is tracked separately.

label: Tension chance within a generated chest injury
description: Chance that a newly generated penetrating chest injury begins with tension. Tension reduces perfusion and requires the appropriate decompression treatment.

label: Maximum initial traumatic lung collapse fraction
description: Initial collapsed fraction of the affected lung after a generated chest injury. Higher values reduce available lung capacity more severely.

label: Internal injury chance at full penetrating impact
description: Chance that an eligible penetrating impact generates an internal bleeding source. Internal blood loss is separate from native external bleeding and cannot be stopped by a dressing.

label: Maximum initial internal source flow (game ml per second)
description: Maximum generated internal blood-loss rate used when scaling injury severity. Higher values make severe internal injuries deteriorate more quickly.

label: Airway contamination chance at full head impact
description: Chance that an eligible head injury causes a soft-tissue or foreign-material airway problem. The required treatment depends on the obstruction type.

label: Generate soft-tissue airway obstruction while unconscious
description: Enable automatic soft-tissue airway obstruction during unconsciousness. This is separate from impact-generated obstruction; an adjunct and ventilation have different functions.

label: Maximum procedure equipment preparation time (seconds)
description: Maximum time allowed to equip the item or enter the required treatment animation. Preparation is separate from the treatment timer; failed preparation retains the reserved supply.

label: Procedure animation completion grace (seconds)
description: Extra time allowed for native animation completion and release around a timed procedure. This prevents a small animation delay from consuming supplies for a failed treatment.

label: Medic time reduction (%)
description: Percentage removed from examination and treatment time for characters assigned the medic role. At 40 percent, a 15-second action takes 9 seconds; this does not speed up physiological recovery.

label: Only medics may perform surgery
description: Restrict extraction, suturing and surgical repairs to assigned medics. Other medical eligibility and facility rules still apply; basic bandaging and splinting remain separate.

label: Only medics may operate AEDs
description: Restrict AED pad application, analysis and discharge to assigned medics. Turning this off permits ordinary characters to use available equipment under the normal rhythm and safety checks.

label: Only medics may insert IVs and administer fluids
description: Restrict vascular-access insertion and fluid administration to assigned medics. This does not change fluid volume, application duration or the need for established access.

label: Only medics may perform advanced airway procedures
description: Restrict adjunct insertion, suction, needle decompression and chest drains to assigned medics. Basic chest sealing and BVM support retain their own normal eligibility rules.

label: Only medics may administer injectable medication
description: Restrict injectable medication administration to assigned medics. Repeat intervals, exact inventory supply and dose-stacking rules still apply.

label: Pulse oximeter setup time (seconds)
description: Base time to start continuous handheld pulse oximetry. The operator must retain the exact device and remain near the patient; the medic time reduction applies.

label: Pulse oximeter operating range (metres)
description: Maximum operator-to-patient separation during handheld monitoring. Monitoring stops when the operator leaves this range, loses the original device or loses examination access.

label: Pulse oximeter audible range (metres)
description: Distance within which nearby players hear the oximeter pulse beep. Beep intervals follow the replicated pulse; cardiac arrest does not produce normal pulse beeps.

label: Pulse oximeter sound enabled
description: Enable pulse-synchronised oximeter beeps for nearby players. Disabling sound keeps numerical live readings available in the Circulation tab.

label: TXA administration time (seconds)
description: Base time for injectable TXA administration. The exact item is consumed only after successful animation and server completion; the medic time reduction applies.

label: TXA onset time (seconds)
description: Time for TXA to reach its maximum simulated clot-stabilising effect. This game-tuned curve does not stop uncontrolled bleeding or replace lost blood.

label: TXA effect duration (seconds)
description: Time over which TXA fades after reaching full effect. Longer values preserve clot-stabilising support for longer; suturing remains a separate procedure.

label: TXA clot breakdown reduction
description: Maximum reduction in movement-related dressing/clot wear while TXA is fully active. A value of 0.5 halves wear; open bleeding sources, fractures and internal injuries still need their own treatment.

label: TXA minimum repeat interval (seconds)
description: Minimum interval before the same patient can receive another TXA administration. The separate maximum-active-dose control can prevent repeat administration even after this interval.

label: TXA maximum active administrations
description: Maximum simultaneous active TXA administrations in one patient. Repeated doses cannot stack clot-stabilising effect beyond its configured maximum.

label: TXA requires vascular access
description: Require established BCM IV access before injectable TXA can be given. Disabling this permits the simplified field-injection workflow; an existing injury is still required.

label: TXA restricted to medics
description: Allow only assigned medics to administer TXA when enabled. The general injectable-medication restriction and vascular-access requirement also apply independently.

label: Two-player stretcher carrying
description: Allow two different players to reserve opposite stretcher ends and lift together. Disabling this safely sets down any carried stretcher and releases both carriers.

label: Stretcher handle reach (metres)
description: Maximum distance from a player to their chosen end handle when joining. Both carriers must remain close enough to opposite ends; standing beside the middle does not reserve an end.

label: Wait for second stretcher carrier (seconds)
description: How long the first carrier can reserve an end while waiting for a second player. Walking away, disconnecting or becoming incapacitated releases the reservation sooner.

label: Minimum carrier separation (metres)
description: Minimum horizontal separation of the two carriers during transport. Coming too close safely sets the stretcher down rather than compressing the casualty or flipping its orientation.

label: Maximum carrier separation (metres)
description: Maximum horizontal separation of the two carriers. Moving farther apart releases both grips and sets down the casualty at the latest supported clear position.

label: Stretcher carry safety speed (metres/second)
description: Transport stops if either carrier exceeds this measured speed. This is an additional safety limit alongside the movement speed fraction; sprinting, jumping or raising a weapon also stops carrying.

label: Stretcher carrier movement fraction
description: Fraction of normal maximum movement speed allowed while both players carry. Existing fracture movement restrictions still apply when they are stricter; the cap is removed on release.

label: Stretcher lift height (metres)
description: Extra height of the stretcher above its supported ground position while carried. The casualty remains on the canvas; this does not change clinical blood or oxygen values.

label: Maximum carrier height difference (metres)
description: Maximum height difference between carrier feet. Greater differences, missing ground or blocked movement stop transport rather than pulling the casualty through terrain or over a ledge.

label: Stretcher movement protection
description: Treat a supported stretcher casualty as resting for movement-related wound wear and fracture strain. Existing bleeding, internal bleeding sources, hypoxia and cardiac arrest continue and still need treatment.

label: Stretcher dressing wear reduction
description: Additional fraction of dressing wear prevented while a casualty is supported on a stretcher with movement protection enabled. This improves dressing stability without closing wounds, refilling blood or repairing fractures.

label: Stretcher carrier end offset (metres)
description: Distance from the stretcher centre to each carrier standing position. Keep enough space for character collision at the end of the canvas; increase maximum carrier separation if using a larger stretcher.

label: Stretcher maximum turn rate (degrees/second)
description: Maximum safe change in stretcher heading during transport. Abrupt turns or teleports beyond this limit set it down; ordinary coordinated turns remain supported and full-length sweeps check the rotation path.

label: Stretcher hand-grip animation
description: Align carrier arms and closed hands to the stretcher handles while native walking continues. Disabling this changes presentation only; carrying and safety checks still apply.

label: Stretcher grip blend time (seconds)
description: Time used to blend the carrier arms into the handle grip. This affects visual entry into the pose and does not change treatment times or the server carry limits.

label: Applied medical equipment visuals
description: Display applied medical devices on character bones using the replicated treatment state. This is cosmetic: disabling it does not remove equipment effects or restore consumed supplies.

label: Applied equipment display range (metres)
description: Maximum viewer distance for applied equipment models. Increase it to see details farther away; lower it to reduce cosmetic work in busy scenes.

label: Show applied leg splints
description: Show a shaped splint on a leg after successful splint application. A splint supports the fracture; the visual does not imply that the bone has healed.

label: Show applied chest devices
description: Display chest seals and AED electrode pads after they have been applied. Device appearance follows patient state and is cleared by authoritative removal or reset.

label: Show applied IV access
description: Show the applied cannula at the recorded access limb. It appears after access is established and does not create an extra usable inventory item.

label: Show applied tourniquets
description: Show an applied tourniquet on each treated limb while the native tourniquet state is active. Removing the treatment or disabling this visual removes the cosmetic strap.

label: Medication vital-sign safeguards
description: Reject medication when the current server vital signs fail its safety checks. The checks are repeated during treatment; disabling this permits risky administration but does not remove physiological effects.

label: Morphine minimum pulse (bpm)
description: Lowest pulse accepted for morphine administration. A slower pulse blocks another dose so the medic can assess circulation and respiratory depression first.

label: Morphine minimum systolic pressure
description: Minimum systolic pressure for morphine. Below this value the server retains the kit and rejects treatment because further opioid-related pressure reduction could worsen perfusion.

label: Morphine minimum breathing rate
description: Minimum spontaneous breaths per minute for morphine. Slow breathing blocks additional opioid administration; ventilation and reversal remain separate treatments.

label: Morphine minimum oxygen saturation
description: Minimum oxygen saturation for another morphine dose, expressed as a fraction. The default 0.90 corresponds to 90 percent; this is a configurable game safeguard.

label: Epinephrine maximum pulse (bpm)
description: Reject epinephrine in a patient with a pulse at or above this rate. This does not prohibit indicated resuscitation medication merely because CPR is being performed.

label: Epinephrine maximum systolic pressure
description: Reject epinephrine in a patient with spontaneous circulation at or above this pressure. Arrest has a separate context and still requires CPR and correction of reversible causes.

label: Allow epinephrine with a pulse
description: Allow the simplified game injector in patients who still have a pulse, subject to the pulse and pressure limits. Disable this for an arrest-only injector policy; it is not a real drug dosing protocol.

label: Naloxone requires active opioid
description: Require an active morphine dose before administering naloxone. Reversal affects opioid-related effects only and cannot repair trauma, replenish blood or resolve an obstructed airway.

label: Fluid vital-sign safeguards
description: Check current systolic pressure and actual native blood deficit before and throughout fluid administration. Unsafe or unnecessary infusions are rejected without deliberately causing an artificial arrest.

label: Fluid stop systolic pressure
description: Stop or reject the simplified fluid procedure at this systolic pressure. This limits unnecessary resuscitation; pressure alone is not simulated as an instant cardiac arrest trigger.

label: Minimum fluid deficit (ml)
description: Minimum missing native blood reserve before an infusion is permitted. Delivered volume remains capped at the actual deficit, so a full patient cannot receive extra reserve.

label: Minimum adequate ventilation rate
description: Spontaneous breathing below this rate progressively reduces the oxygen target. An ordinary modest opioid-related slowdown does not automatically produce profound hypoxia; BVM can support ventilation.

label: Blood-loss compensation pulse boost
description: Maximum pulse increase driven by falling blood reserve before decompensation. Blood loss, pain and stimulants contribute separately; late severe shock can then slow the heart.

label: Maximum pain pulse increase
description: Maximum additional beats per minute from untreated perceived pain. Analgesia reduces this contribution through the same pain model used for aiming effects.

label: Late shock decompensation fraction
description: Below this fraction of normal blood reserve, compensatory heart rate starts to fail. This links late bradycardia to severe shock rather than making every slow pulse fatal.

label: Lower efficient pumping rate
description: Below this pulse, the model progressively reduces pumping efficiency and pressure. It is a game abstraction of inadequate cardiac output, not a universal clinical cutoff.

label: Upper efficient pumping rate
description: Above this pulse, progressively reduced filling lowers pumping efficiency. High pulse becomes dangerous through perfusion and pressure, rather than an arbitrary immediate kill.

label: Critical slow pulse threshold
description: A pulse at or below this threshold contributes to arrest only alongside poor pressure for the configured exposure time. A healthy low resting pulse alone does not trigger arrest.

label: Critical fast pulse threshold
description: A pulse at or above this threshold contributes to arrest only with poor pressure sustained for the configured exposure time. Resulting pulseless tachycardia is assessed by the AED rhythm rules.

label: Critical perfusion pressure
description: Sustained systolic pressure at or below this value can lead to nonshockable arrest, including unresolved tension or severe drug-related compromise. Duration is controlled separately.

label: Rate instability pressure ceiling
description: Rate-extreme arrest requires pressure below this value as well as the slow or fast pulse threshold. This distinguishes instability from a numerical heart-rate alarm alone.

label: Unstable vital exposure time (seconds)
description: How long critical pressure or a compromised extreme pulse must persist before arrest. Correcting the cause resets this timer; a brief transient does not automatically cause arrest.

label: TXA internal clot support fraction
description: Maximum reduction in ongoing internal blood loss at full TXA effect. TXA does not repair the source, remove a projectile, drain collected blood or replace external bleeding control.

label: Allow native passive blood regeneration
description: Allow the base game to regenerate missing blood reserve passively after its native delay. Disabled by default so controlling bleeding does not automatically replace lost reserve; finite fluid treatment remains separate.

label: Simulate fluid composition
description: Track volume, red-cell reserve and clotting support separately. Saline supports volume, plasma also supports clotting, and whole blood also restores oxygen-carrying reserve; disabling this uses the legacy shared-reserve behaviour.

label: Saline retained volume fraction
description: Fraction of an infused saline bag retained after the simplified redistribution phase. The remaining volume leaves the native circulating reserve over the configured redistribution time; this does not remove red cells.

label: Plasma retained volume fraction
description: Fraction of infused plasma volume retained after simplified redistribution. Plasma restores clotting support but does not supply red cells or directly increase their oxygen-carrying reserve.

label: Fluid redistribution time scale (seconds)
description: Time scale for unretained non-blood fluid to redistribute out of circulation. This is a gradual exponential game abstraction; it changes reserve and pressure without creating a bleeding wound.

label: Maximum dilution bleeding increase
description: Maximum additional internal bleeding multiplier when clotting support is severely diluted. Plasma or whole blood can improve the deficit, but neither repairs an open internal source.

label: Maximum dilution dressing wear increase
description: Maximum extra dressing wear caused by diluted clotting support. TXA can support clot persistence, while plasma replenishes clotting reserve; closure remains a separate procedure.

label: Critical oxygen-delivery fraction
description: Sustained inadequate oxygen delivery can cause nonshockable arrest even with normal SpO2. Delivery includes perfusion and red-cell reserve; a pulse oximeter alone cannot diagnose adequate tissue oxygen transport.

label: Recovery oxygen-delivery fraction
description: Minimum estimated spontaneous tissue oxygen delivery before the ROSC stability timer can advance. Correcting pressure with cell-free fluid alone does not replace severely lost red-cell reserve.

label: Portable oxygen enabled
description: Enable portable oxygen sessions. Disabling stops supply without changing the underlying airway, chest injury or blood reserve.

label: Connect oxygen equipment (seconds)
description: Base time to connect the retained portable oxygen kit to a patient. Movement, loss of access or role changes cancel before supply starts.

label: Disconnect oxygen equipment (seconds)
description: Base time to disconnect an active oxygen session. The retained device keeps its remaining capacity and can be used again.

label: New portable oxygen capacity (litres)
description: Capacity assigned when a new oxygen kit spawns. Used oxygen is not replenished by reconnecting or transferring the same device.

label: Portable oxygen flow (litres/minute)
description: Flow consumed from the exact retained device while connected, including when the airway is obstructed. Empty devices stop supplying oxygen.

label: Oxygen operator maximum range (metres)
description: The operator must retain the exact device within this distance of the patient. Separation, device loss, death or a reset disconnects supply.

label: Oxygen support of remaining lung capacity
description: Simplified oxygenation benefit for functioning lung tissue. It does not reinflate a lung, relieve tension, provide breaths or replace missing red cells.

label: Minimum lung fraction for oxygen benefit
description: Below this functioning-lung fraction oxygen cannot improve the saturation target. Airway patency and ventilation are checked separately.

label: Oxygen connection requires medic
description: Restrict connecting and disconnecting oxygen equipment to the server-assigned medic role. Revalidation during connection uses the live setting.

label: Show applied oxygen mask
description: Show a cosmetic mask while oxygen is connected. This visibility control changes presentation only; supply and clinical effects remain authoritative.

label: Tablet administration time (seconds)
description: Base time to administer the oral tablet supply. An unresponsive patient or unsafe swallowing conditions reject or interrupt the procedure.

label: Paracetamol onset (game seconds)
description: Time to peak of the slower oral analgesic game effect. Pain can persist during onset; this does not represent a real clinical dose schedule.

label: Paracetamol clearance (game seconds)
description: Time for tablet analgesia to fade after its peak. This abstract model does not simulate liver chemistry or make overdose safe.

label: Tablet minimum repeat interval (seconds)
description: Authority-enforced minimum time between oral supplies. Combined with the active-dose cap to prevent unlimited repeated administration.

label: Maximum active tablet administrations
description: Maximum concurrent tablet game doses. These are abstract supplies, not a real-world tablet count or prescribing limit.

label: Tablet pain relief (game units)
description: Pain reduction at peak strength. Tablets do not repair injuries, refill reserve or reverse opioid effects.

label: Minimum breathing rate for oral medicine
description: Oral medication requires spontaneous circulation, an open airway, this minimum breathing rate and an actually conscious native character.

label: Fentanyl administration (seconds)
description: Base time for the finite injectable game supply. The procedure rechecks role, vascular access and vital limits until completion.

label: Fentanyl analgesic onset (game seconds)
description: Time to peak analgesia for the faster opioid option. Breathing depression has a separately configured onset and can outlast pain relief.

label: Fentanyl analgesic clearance (seconds)
description: Time for fentanyl analgesia to fade after its peak. This is compressed game timing and does not remove residual respiratory risk.

label: Fentanyl breathing-effect onset (seconds)
description: Time to peak opioid breathing and pressure effects. These add to morphine exposure and share naloxone reversal.

label: Fentanyl breathing-effect clearance (seconds)
description: Clearance time for residual opioid effects, independent of analgesic clearance. Reassess even after pain relief has faded.

label: Fentanyl minimum repeat interval (seconds)
description: Minimum interval between fentanyl game administrations. Active-dose limits and live clinical safety checks also apply.

label: Maximum active fentanyl administrations
description: Cap concurrent fentanyl exposures. Residual breathing effects keep an exposure active after its analgesia has faded.

label: Fentanyl pain relief (game units)
description: Peak analgesic effect of the stronger short-acting option. Analgesia does not stop bleeding or repair injury.

label: Fentanyl breathing depression fraction
description: Peak reduction of spontaneous ventilation from one active game exposure. Morphine and fentanyl risks accumulate before shared reversal.

label: Fentanyl pressure depression fraction
description: Peak reduction of simulated pressure support. A low-volume patient can deteriorate despite apparent pain improvement.

label: Fentanyl minimum systolic pressure
description: Withhold this opioid below the configured systolic pressure. This is a game safeguard, not a universal clinical prescribing threshold.

label: Fentanyl minimum pulse (bpm)
description: Withhold fentanyl below this pulse or without spontaneous circulation. Other vital and route restrictions remain active.

label: Fentanyl minimum breathing rate
description: Withhold fentanyl below this breathing rate. A pulse oximeter alone cannot exclude developing respiratory depression.

label: Fentanyl minimum oxygen fraction
description: Withhold fentanyl below this saturation when vital safeguards are enabled. Revalidation can cancel an unsafe administration without consuming it.

label: Fentanyl requires vascular access
description: Require established access for the injectable fentanyl game route. No real milligram or microgram dosing is represented.

label: Fentanyl requires medic
description: Restrict this stronger opioid to the server-assigned medic role, independently of the general medication permission.

label: Medical supply refund fraction
description: Fraction of the current medical supply cost returned on deposit. Default zero avoids refunding used oxygen or discharged equipment as a fresh item.

label: Mask right offset (m)
description: Move the applied mask sideways relative to the animated head.

label: Mask up offset (m)
description: Move the applied mask vertically relative to the animated head. This is cosmetic and does not affect oxygen delivery.

label: Mask forward offset (m)
description: Adjust face clearance for helmets and facial geometry. Uses the head frame rather than the torso.

label: Mask scale
description: Uniform size of the supplied mask and reservoir. Cosmetic scale does not change gas capacity or flow.

label: Mask yaw adjustment
description: Rotate the applied mask around the head vertical axis for donor-model fitting.

label: Mask pitch adjustment
description: Correct the donor model axis and face angle. Default ninety degrees aligns its original flat mesh with the face.

label: Mask roll adjustment
description: Rotate the applied mask around the face-forward axis. This affects appearance only.

label: Tablet hand-to-mouth animation
description: Use the original BCM tablet animation on supported poses. Disabling it uses the native handling fallback; clinical timing, swallowing guards and supply consumption still apply.

label: Allow body-bag burial
description: Allow timed burial of a named world body bag with a real US or USSR shovel. Disabling this cancels active digging and preserves the bag.

label: Body-bag burial duration (seconds)
description: Time required to dig one grave. The duration is captured when digging begins; range, shovel and player-session checks continue until commit.

label: Body-bag burial range (metres)
description: Maximum performer distance from the exact body bag throughout digging. Moving out of range cancels without disposing the bag.

label: Allow sending body bags home
description: Allow authoritative return-home disposition for a ready world body bag inside an enabled native healing station area. Equipment already deposited in a vehicle stays in that vehicle.

label: Allow stabilised blood-component recovery
description: Enable gradual recovery of diluted red-cell and clotting reserves in a stabilised patient. This never adds circulating blood volume, repairs wounds or replaces emergency transfusion. Disabled by default; native passive blood-volume regeneration remains a separate policy.

label: Red-cell recovery timescale (seconds)
description: After this much eligible game time, about 63 percent of the existing red-cell deficit has recovered. A larger value slows recovery. This never adds missing circulating blood volume.

label: Clotting recovery timescale (seconds)
description: After this much eligible game time, about 63 percent of the existing clotting deficit has recovered. A larger value slows recovery. This does not close bleeding sources, remove pooled blood or replace surgical repair.

label: Minimum volume for component recovery
description: Minimum native circulating blood fraction before gradual component recovery is allowed. Below this threshold, replace missing volume and control bleeding first.

label: Require facility for component recovery
description: Require the patient to remain within the configured range of an active stationary medical facility. Leaving the facility pauses recovery; portable supply items do not count as facilities.

label: Minimum pressure for component recovery
description: Minimum game systolic pressure for gradual component recovery. Low pressure pauses recovery so it cannot substitute for treating shock.

label: Allow independent fluid drips
description: Adds separate drip connection actions. The original finite bag moves into patient inventory and follows the patient while the medic leaves. Requires space and existing access. Disabling stops active lines without refilling bags.

label: Fluid line connection time (seconds)
description: Time to connect an existing finite bag to the selected vascular access. The bag remains unchanged if connection is cancelled before transfer. Subsequent flow uses the existing full-bag infusion duration.

label: Fluid line disconnection time (seconds)
description: Time to disconnect the current line. No spare bag is needed. The original bag and any remaining contents stay in the patient's inventory.

label: Model redistributed fluid overload
description: Opt-in normalized game burden from typed-fluid water leaving circulation. It can impair lung capacity without creating tension or pleural blood. Disabling stops new accumulation/effects; stored burden still clears during active simulated time.

label: Fluid burden onset fraction
description: Normalized redistributed-fluid burden at which breathing effects begin. Fractions use the GM normal blood-volume scale and are gameplay values. Must remain below the severe burden fraction.

label: Severe fluid burden fraction
description: Normalized burden at maximum configured lung impairment. Must remain above the onset fraction. Increasing this requires more retained burden for severe effects.

label: Fluid burden clearance timescale
description: Active-game clearance timescale at full spontaneous perfusion: about63 percent of existing burden clears in one timescale. Poor perfusion slows clearance; arrest and offline time award none. This does not refill native blood volume.

label: Lung fraction at severe fluid burden
description: Multiplier on remaining structural lung capacity at severe burden. Lower values worsen linked oxygenation. Oxygen and ventilation support do not erase the saved burden; needles and chest drains do not remove it.

label: Withhold additional water-loading fluids
description: With overload and fluid safety checks enabled, stop or withhold saline/plasma at the configured burden severity. Preserve remaining finite bag contents. Whole blood still follows the existing access, pressure and volume guards.

label: Water-loading stop severity
description: Severity between onset0 and severe1 at which further saline/plasma loading is withheld. Zero stops once burden is above onset; it never blocks a burden-free patient or a disabled overload model.

label: Progress-only splint, surgery and suturing
description: Use the authoritative timer and on-screen progress for splinting, extraction, suturing and internal/fracture surgery instead of custom treatment clips. Preserves clinical eligibility, original supply reservation and cancellation. Native bandaging and injectable presentation remain separate. Changes apply to new procedures.

0: native drop. 1: retain the original held rifle, sniper rifle or machine gun only with a sling in inventory. 2: retain those weapons without requiring a sling. One held weapon only; grenades, pistols and launchers keep native handling. No weapon is cloned.

description: Supply cost of the inventory-only weapon sling in BCM Medical faction arsenals.

Living casualty carrying
description: Allow carrying a living casualty. Conscious players must accept through the medical panel; unconscious casualties need no consent prompt.

label: Living casualty dragging
description: Allow crouched slow dragging of living casualties. Conscious players must accept; unconscious casualties need no consent prompt.
Maximum server-verified distance to request and start carry or drag.
label: Casualty pickup and request range

description: Maximum native movement-speed fraction while carrying. No sprint, jump or vault.
label: Casualty carry movement fraction

description: Maximum native movement-speed fraction while dragging; the rescuer stays crouched and can turn freely.
label: Casualty crouch-drag movement fraction

description: Release transport if a rescuer moves farther than this between authority updates; prevents teleport catch-up.
